predecessors.name: Duchy of Lower Lorraine
predecessors.text: 'The county emerged about 1096 when the first documented reference to Gerard III of Wassenberg' as Count of Guelders appeared

successors.name: Habsburg Netherlands
successors.text: 'the definitive acquisition of the Duchy of Guelders and the adjoining County of Zutphen by the House of Habsburg' (Treaty of Venlo, 7 September 1543)

ledger.x: Before 1339 (page silent on the years): Veluwe, Nijmegen, Betuwe, Roermond and Venlo.
1339: duchy. 'In 1339, the Emperor Louis IV of Wittelsbach elevated Count Reginald II of Guelders' to duke.
1538: the end of Charles of Egmond's reign.

wars.name: Guelders War of Succession
wars.outcome: After the Wassenberg line ended in 1371, William I of Jülich won; he was confirmed in 1379 and held both duchies in personal union from 1393.

wars.name: Guelders Wars
wars.outcome: 'The wars lasted from 1502 to 1543 and ended with a Burgundian victory': peace at Gorinchem (3 October 1528), at Grave after the 1536 invasion of Groningen, and the Treaty of Venlo (7 September 1543) giving Guelders and Zutphen to Charles V.

certainty.note: The page gives counts, a marriage in 1127 and no boundaries.
The gazetteer region is a stand-in for the duchy's quarters; the page gives no area or boundary, and the Upper Quarter's extent in particular is approximate.
